reason: This text does not support the statement that violence towards unruly people is the model for good leadership. Instead, the text demonstrates Moses' leadership model: (1) When people complain about bitter water at Marah, Moses appeals to God rather than using force; (2) When people hunger, God provides manna without Moses employing violence; (3) When people thirst at Rephidim, Moses again seeks God's intervention by striking a rock; (4) When Jethro advises Moses on delegating leadership, he emphasizes selecting 'men of valor, fearing God, truthful men, who hate dishonest gain'—emphasizing moral character, not violence; (5) The only military action mentioned (against Amalek) is defensive warfare, not suppression of unruly people. The text consistently shows leadership through faith, divine guidance, moral character, and addressing legitimate needs—not through violence toward the people.
